title: Investigate kernel routing changes causing numerical drift and prefill/decode concurrency issues
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After deploying kernel routing heuristics that prefer low-precision fused attention kernels for specific sequence-length profiles, we observed small but growing differences in model outputs compared to baseline kernels. In some long-running streams the difference grows over time and in rare cases triggers token-level divergences that impact quality-sensitive customers. Separately, a change to prefill/decode scheduling for continuous batching revealed a concurrency window where KV cache entries were transiently overwritten, causing corrupted attention when requests hit a specific timing pattern. This ticket captures the investigation, reproducible cases, mitigations, and PRs for fixes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Checkout runtime-1.21 branch with kernel-routing feature flag enabled
2) Use model rdl-3b-fused-attn-quant with mixed-precision GEMMs and sequence profile: many short prefill calls followed by long decode streams
3) Run long stream workload (10k tokens across multiple sessions) with continuous batching enabled and prefill scheduled on worker thread A while decode uses worker thread B
4) Compare outputs token-by-token vs same workload with kernel-routing disabled and the previous kernel selection policy

5) Observe per-token log-likelihood divergence >1e-3 after ~2000 decode tokens in ~0.6% of sessions and complete token corruption in ~0.02% of sessions when concurrency window aligns with cache eviction.
experiments: A: Baseline kernel selector (prior heuristic) — no drift observed in runs up to 20k tokens
B: New kernel routing with low-precision fused kernels — drift observed; avg per-token LL gap 2.3e-3
C: New routing + single-threaded prefill/decode (serialize scheduling) — drift persisted but corruption eliminated
D: New routing + per-request KV cache mutex — corruption eliminated; throughput drop ~6% measured on p3-8x (benchmarks attached)
E: New routing + atomic pointer swap with epoch counters — reduced lock contention and prevented overwrite in stress tests; still seeing numeric drift
decision_log: 2025-03-06: Revert kernel routing feature flag for affected model families in hosted infra (approved by Sofia Chen) to mitigate customer risk (rollback PR: GH#9243)

2025-03-09: Continue exploring deterministic fallback path for accuracy-critical routes and add low-noise mode for mixed-precision kernels (design doc linked)
